The first episodes will premiere on the Kion streaming service on November 26, with a television premiere on REN TV set for December 6. Bortko reportedly worked on the project for 15 years, and the script is based on declassified documents and memoirs. The story takes place between 1945 and 1953, the year Joseph Stalin died. The filmmakers promise to show “not good or bad, but the truth,” but judging by the trailer, it’s a typical Russian “patriotic blockbuster” in which a resolute leader stands up to the West. Stalin is played by Igor Mirkurbanov, an actor who has mostly played antiheroes onstage, including the Pretender in Boris Godunov and the elder Karamazov in The Karamazovs. The film also stars Viktor Sukhorukov as Khrushchev and Alexander Yatsko as Beria. On November 23, a society premiere of the film was held at Moscow’s Khudozhestvenny movie theater, where invited Russian celebrities posed for photos in front of a press wall bearing the word “STALIN.” Take a look at these photos.
